chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Zayd al-Shahham, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), who said:
No servant says seven times every day, 'I ask God for Paradise, and I seek refuge in God from the Fire,' except that the Fire says: 'O my Lord! Give him refuge from me.'

key_terms.أعوذ بالله: I seek refuge in God; a formula of seeking divine protection
key_terms.الجنة: Paradise (Jannah), the eternal abode of the righteous
key_terms.النار: The Fire (Hellfire), the abode of punishment

ai.seo_question: What daily supplication causes the Fire to ask God to protect you?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a simple daily supplication: asking God for Paradise and seeking refuge from Hellfire, repeated seven times each day. The hadith personifies the Fire itself as interceding on behalf of the supplicant, asking God to protect them. This vivid imagery underscores the power of consistent daily supplication in the Islamic devotional tradition.
